penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Managed/concierge health tracking is inherently a done-for-you service requiring ongoing human judgement to review symptoms, synthesize records, and communicate with patients — per-customer manual work that cannot be fully automated by Claude.

penalties_applied.name: regulated_industry
penalties_applied.reason: Health data management touches HIPAA (US), GDPR health data (EU), and similar regimes globally. Even as a non-clinical service, handling chronic illness patient data carries significant regulatory exposure.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Chronic illness patients and caregivers in distress require responsive, empathetic, human-quality support — not an automated ticketing bot.

rationale: The buyers here are individual consumers managing personal health — a vague, hard-to-reach, low-budget segment that rarely pays for software tools at meaningful price points. Even if willingness to pay exists at the margins, the service is fundamentally a concierge/done-for-you model requiring per-customer human involvement (reviewing symptom logs, synthesising across appointments, fielding patient questions), which makes autonomous delivery impossible. The regulated-industry exposure around health data processing adds compliance risk that a solo non-technical operator cannot absorb.
solution_plan: This idea cannot realistically be built and maintained by a solo non-technical operator. A viable chronic illness tracking service would require clinical oversight, HIPAA-compliant data infrastructure, and per-patient human attention that cannot be automated away. Even a lighter 'AI health diary' product would sit in a regulated grey zone and require ongoing human support that negates the autonomy requirement. Do not pursue.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy (2 < 7), buildability_with_ai (3 < 6), buyer_clarity (3 < 6), and willingness_to_pay (5 = floor but total is below validate threshold after penalties). Regulated industry and human-fulfillment penalties push total below 1.0.
